title: Solid-state battery dendrite suppression
bottleneck: Lithium dendrites pierce solid electrolytes and short-circuit solid-state cells, and a 2026 review found the failure is a cascade, not a single mechanism: grain boundaries with a thousand-fold lower ionic conductivity seed filaments, slow lithium self-diffusion causes voiding that concentrates current, and electronic leakage lets lithium plate inside the ceramic itself. No single fix addresses all pathways at once.
why_it_blocks: Solid-state batteries promise higher energy density and safety than liquid-electrolyte cells, which underpin EVs and grid storage. Dendrite-driven shorting is the central obstacle to commercial viability, keeping the technology in pilot lines after decades of development.
current_state: Recent work traces failure to the crystal level — a 2026 MIT study pinned dendrite origins to charged grain boundaries in LLZO, while Max Planck researchers showed internal stress fractures the ceramic. Dynamic crosslinked polymers that self-heal interfaces are a promising but unproven direction.
